body:
The Korea Investment Corp. is exploring a sale of more than $1 billion in private equity interests on the secondary market, according to reporting by Bloomberg News.

PJT Partners was appointed by the South Korean sovereign wealth fund to advise on the potential transaction. Discussions are at an early stage, noted the report, and the assets involved, transaction structure and potential size could change.

Markets Group has reached out to KIC for comment and is awaiting response.

By the end of 2025, KIC had $232 billion under management and reported a 13.91% investment return in 2025 along with a 10-year annualized return of 7.07%. More than 78% of its portfolio was allocated to traditional assets, including equities and fixed income, with the remainder in alternative investments including private equity and real estate.

KIC isn’t the only fund seeking buyers on the secondary market. In June, GIC was reported to be finalizing a sale of as much as $2 billion of private credit assets, with Evercore advising, according to Bloomberg. The sale is part of a broader effort by the sovereign wealth fund to recycle capital across private market strategies. The following month, GIC Chief Executive Officer Lim Chow Kiat said in an interview with Bloomberg that the fund had become more cautious about private market investments and was actively recycling capital across private market strategies. In September, Ardian agreed to acquire the portfolio after making a preemptive offer at a premium to book value, according to subsequent reporting by Bloomberg.

The broader secondary market has also been expanding rapidly. Global secondary transaction volume reached about $121 billion in the first half of 2026, up 19% from the same period in 2025 and the strongest first half on record, according to Evercore’s H1 2026 Secondary Market Review. GP-led transactions accounted for $65 billion, while LP-led transactions totaled $56 billion. Evercore said full-year volume is tracking toward roughly $250 billion to $260 billion.
